article_title: Recent rainfall predicts broader frog acoustic participation without stronger residual co-calling associations
supported_claims: Across independent North American and Australian acoustic monitoring systems, more recent rainfall is associated with a greater probability of multispecies frog calling in short observation units.
In NAAMP, the rain association remains negative after temperature adjustment and after additional nonlinear day-of-year adjustment.
Within-space diagnostics in NAAMP and FrogID retain the same rain direction, so static spatial differences in local species pools are insufficient to explain the association.
In NAAMP, more recent rain is associated with greater acoustic activation and a larger acoustically active species pool.

In NAAMP, rain does not detectably strengthen multispecies calling conditional on acoustic activity, observed-minus-independence residual co-calling, mean pairwise excess covariance, or pairwise network density.
The hierarchy-corrected seasonal-shoulder interaction remains unsupported.

interpretation.strongest: The NAAMP multispecies rainfall signal is activation-dominated: broader acoustic participation is detected without detectable strengthening of residual co-calling association.
interpretation.cross_system_limit: FrogID independently validates the raw event-level multispecies rainfall association, not the activation-versus-residual-association decomposition.
interpretation.general_implication: Multispecies co-activity should not by itself be interpreted as synchrony, facilitation, or temporal-niche reorganization.
